320716.title: Optimal precoding matrices conjecture for slow-fading MIMO channels
320716.statement:
Let $\Gamma(\mathbf{Q},R)$ denote the goodput-to-power ratio, let $P_{\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{Q},R)$ denote the outage probability, and let $\overline{P}$ be the available transmit-power constraint. Let $n_t$ be the number of transmit antennas and let $\mathbf{I}_{n_t}$ be the $n_t\times n_t$ identity matrix. **Optimal precoding matrices conjecture.** There exists a power threshold $\overline{P}_0$ such that:

- if $\overline{P}\leq\overline{P}_0$, then

$$
\mathbf{Q}^*\in\arg\min_{\mathbf{Q}}P_{\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{Q},R)\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathbf{Q}^*\in\arg\max_{\mathbf{Q}}\Gamma(\mathbf{Q},R);
$$

- if $\overline{P}>\overline{P}_0$, then $\Gamma(\mathbf{Q},R)$ has a unique maximum at

$$
\mathbf{Q}^*=\frac{p^*}{n_t}\mathbf{I}_{n_t},\qquad p^*\leq\overline{P}.
$$

The conjecture has been validated for all the special cases solved in the paper. It says that below the threshold, maximizing the goodput-to-power ratio is equivalent to minimizing outage probability, whereas above the threshold uniform power allocation is optimal and using all available power is generally suboptimal for energy efficiency.
320716.source_name: E. V. Belmega and S. Lasaulce, “Energy-Efficient Precoding for Multiple-Antenna Terminals”, arXiv:1011.4597 (2010).
320716.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4597

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

321551.title: The existence conjecture for p-extremal elementary graphs
321551.statement: Let $p\geq1$ be an integer. A $p$-extremal elementary graph is an elementary graph with $p$ perfect matchings and maximum possible excess $c_p$. **p-extremal elementary-graph existence conjecture.** For every $p\geq1$, there exists a $p$-extremal elementary graph. The source says that all known values of $p$ admit such graphs, but does not establish the assertion in general.
321551.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

325977.title: Hähnle's connected layer multicomplex diameter conjecture
325977.statement:
Let $H_{\operatorname{c.l.m.}}(n,d)$ be the maximum length of a connected layer multicomplex of rank $d$ on $n$ elements. **Hähnle's conjecture.** For all $n$ and $d$,

$$
H_{\operatorname{c.l.m.}}(n,d)\leq d(n-1).
$$

This is a multicomplex generalization proposed in the Polymath 3 project. The source does not report a resolution of the conjecture.
325977.source_name: Francisco Santos, “Recent progress on the combinatorial diameter of polytopes and simplicial complexes”, arXiv:1307.5900 (2013).
325977.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.5900

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2013). “The conjecture itself has been disproved, but what we know about the underlying question is quite scarce.”

330632.title: Prime-power Olson degree conjecture
330632.statement: An integer $d$ is an **Olson degree** if every torsion subgroup of a CM elliptic curve defined over a number field of degree $d$ is determined by the curve's CM data as in the paper. **Prime-power Olson degree conjecture.** $p^n$ is an Olson degree for every prime $p>5$ and all $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. The conjecture strengthens the stated prime-power theorem and is supported computationally: no counterexample with $p>5$ was found for $p^n\leq 10^{14}$ unconditionally, or for $p^n\leq 10^{30}$ using computations conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. It remains open in general.
330632.source_name: Abbey Bourdon, Pete L. Clark and Paul Pollack, “Anatomy of torsion in the CM case”, arXiv:1506.00565 (2015).
330632.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.00565

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

332532.title: Bezdek–Zamfirescu's X-ray conjecture
332532.statement:
Let $X(\mathbf{K})$ be the smallest number of lines such that every boundary point of a convex body $\mathbf{K}$ is X-rayed along at least one of them. **X-ray conjecture.** For every convex body $\mathbf{K}\subset\mathbb{E}^d$,

$$
X(\mathbf{K})\leq 3\cdot 2^{d-2}.
$$

The conjecture is proved in the plane but remains open in higher dimensions.
332532.source_name: Karoly Bezdek and Muhammad A. Khan, “The geometry of homothetic covering and illumination”, arXiv:1602.06040 (2016).
332532.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.06040

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2016). “The X-ray Conjecture is proved only in the plane and it is open in higher dimensions.”

333719.title: The degree-associated edge-reconstruction conjecture for trees
333719.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $dern(T)$ denote the minimum number of degree-associated edge-cards needed to determine $T$ up to isomorphism. **Degree-associated edge-reconstruction conjecture.** For every tree $T$,

$$
dern(T)\leq 2.
$$

The paper supports this with results for caterpillars, star-like trees, and several other tree families, but the assertion for all trees remains open.
333719.source_name: Kevin J. Asciak, “The degree-associated edge-reconstruction number of disconnected graphs and trees”, arXiv:1608.01158 (2016).
333719.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.01158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2016).

335702.title: Born winner/silver spoon regime conjecture for the multiplicative coalescent
335702.statement:
Let $(\boldsymbol{x}^{\scriptscriptstyle(n)})_{n\geqslant 1}$ satisfy Condition II$\tau$ for some $\tau\in(3,4)$, and let $M_n$ be as in the leader theorem. Write $\mathcal{W}_n$ for the event that the component containing $x_1^{\scriptscriptstyle(n)}$ is always the leader, meaning that the identity of the leader never changes. Assume $c_1>c_2$. **Born winner/silver spoon regime conjecture.** There exists $\delta>0$ such that

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(M_n^-\geqslant K)>\delta
$$

for every $K>0$. Moreover,

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(\mathcal{W}_n)>0.
$$

The first assertion predicts that, under Condition II$\tau$, the negative part of the leader-stabilization time is not tight, complementing the tightness result for its positive part. The second asserts a positive limiting probability that the component containing the largest initial particle remains leader forever; both claims are left conjectural in the stated regime.
335702.source_name: Louigi Addario-Berry, Shankar Bhamidi and Sanchayan Sen, “A probabilistic approach to the leader problem in random graphs”, arXiv:1703.09908 (2020).
335702.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.09908

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

342519.title: Sottile–Williams conjecture on simple Bruhat interval polytopes
342519.statement: Let $v,w\in\mathfrak{S}_n$ with $v\leq w$, and let $Q_{v,w}$ be the Bruhat interval polytope whose vertices are the permutations $u\in[v,w]$. For each $u\in[v,w]$, let $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ be the transitive reduction of the acyclic graph associated with the vertex $u$; by the preceding proposition, $u$ is simple in $Q_{v,w}$ exactly when the underlying undirected graph of $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ is a forest. **Sottile–Williams conjecture.** The polytope $Q_{v,w}$ is simple if and only if the vertices $v$ and $w$ are simple. Equivalently, if the graphs $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_v$ and $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_v$ are forests, then $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ is a forest for every $v\leq u\leq w$. This generalizes Conjecture 7.16 of Le–Ma, which concerns the corresponding case with the lower endpoint equal to the identity permutation. The conjecture asserts that checking simplicity at the endpoints suffices to determine simplicity of the entire Bruhat interval polytope.
342519.source_name: Eunjeong Lee, Mikiya Masuda and Seonjeong Park, “Toric Bruhat interval polytopes”, arXiv:1904.10187 (2019).
342519.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

355819.title: Component-count conjecture for $X_9^2$ singularities
355819.statement:
Let $f_0$ be a real function singularity of type $X_9^2$. Consider the discriminant variety in the parameter space of an arbitrary versal deformation of $f_0$. The indicated representatives are those shown in Fig. X92, together with their negatives and their rotations through multiples of $\pi/2$.

**$X_9^2$ component conjecture.** These representatives exhaust the components of the complement of the discriminant variety; in total there are 52 such components.

The preceding proposition gives 18 virtual components, arranged into nine pairs, and describes the symmetry operations used to construct the proposed representatives. The conjecture asserts that these constructions account for every actual discriminant-complement component.
355819.source_name: V. A. Vassiliev, “Complements of discriminants of real parabolic function singularities”, arXiv:2208.10929 (2023).
355819.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0909.0062](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0062).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10929

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

355935.title: Amended Gaussian optimality conjecture for the Han–Kobayashi region
355935.statement: Let $(N_1,N_2,u,q_1,q_2)$ denote positive channel and power parameters, and let the **isotropic condition** mean that the maximum in the stated theorem is achieved by isotropic Gaussian inputs for every positive integer dimension. Let 1-letter HKGS without power control and 1-letter HKGS with power control denote the corresponding Gaussian Han–Kobayashi schemes. **Amended Gaussian optimality conjecture.** The set of $(N_1,N_2,u,q_1,q_2)$ satisfying the isotropic condition in the theorem equals the set of parameters for which 1-letter HKGS without power control matches 1-letter HKGS with power control. This conjecture isolates the stability regime in which power control is unnecessary for the Gaussian Han–Kobayashi bound. The paper states that the isotropic parameter set is nonempty and that a more precise characterization remains open; its status evidence says that disproving this conjecture would disprove optimality of HKGS with power control for the whole capacity region.
355935.source_name: Jingbo Liu, “Stability of the Gaussian Stationary Point in the Han-Kobayashi Region for Z-Interference Channels”, arXiv:2209.00163 (2022).
355935.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00163

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2022).

356592.title: The list-coloring conjecture for squares of planar graphs of maximum degree four
356592.statement:
Let $G^2$ denote the square of a planar graph $G$, let $\chi_\ell$ denote list chromatic number, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$.

**List-coloring conjecture.** For every planar graph $G$ satisfying $\Delta(G) \le 4$,

$$
\chi_\ell(G^2) \le 12.
$$

The paper proves the corresponding bound for planar graphs of maximum degree four without five-cycles and identifies this statement as future work for general planar graphs of maximum degree four.
356592.source_name: Eric Culver and Stephen G. Hartke, “Square of Planar Graphs of Max Degree Four without Five Cycles”, arXiv:2210.13618 (2022).
356592.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13618

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

356625.title: Degree-three irrationality conjecture for eight Fano threefold deformation families
356625.statement:
Let $X_d$ be a quasismooth member of one of the eight deformation families numbered \textnumero 1, \textnumero 19, \textnumero 28, \textnumero 39, \textnumero 49, \textnumero 59, \textnumero 66, and \textnumero 84. Let $\mathrm{d}(X_d)$ denote the smallest degree of a generically finite dominant rational map from $X_d$ to projective space of the same dimension. **Degree-three irrationality conjecture.** For every such $X_d$, 

$$
\mathrm{d}(X_d)=3.
$$

The surrounding theorem states this for a general member of each of the eight families, while the candidate extends the assertion to every quasismooth member; the status of this stronger formulation is not established by the supplied context.
356625.source_name: Ivan Cheltsov and Jihun Park, “Degree of irrationality of Fano threefold hypersurfaces”, arXiv:2210.14777 (2022).
356625.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.14777

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

357230.title: Conjecture on the induced forest number of Paley graphs of square order
357230.statement:
Let $q>7$ be a prime power, and let $\mathcal{P}(q^2)$ denote the Paley graph on the finite field of order $q^2$. Let $\tau(G)$ denote the maximum order of an induced forest in a graph $G$. **Induced forest conjecture.** For $q>7$ a prime power,

$$
\tau(\mathcal{P}(q^2))=q+1.
$$

The preceding computational searches found that adding two vertices to a maximum independent set does not produce a forest for all prime powers $7<q\leq 67$, suggesting that the smaller examples are anomalies. The conjecture predicts the exact maximum induced-forest order for Paley graphs of square order beyond these small cases.
357230.source_name: Karen Gunderson, Karen Meagher, Joy Morris and Venkata Raghu Tej Pantangi, “Induced forests in some distance-regular graphs”, arXiv:2301.05207 (2023).
357230.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05207

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

358866.title: The DET:OLD density conjecture for $C_4$-free cubic graphs
358866.statement:
Let $G$ be a $C_4$-free cubic graph, and let $\textrm{DET:OLD}\%(G)$ denote the minimum density of an error-detecting open-locating-dominating set in $G$. **DET:OLD density conjecture.**

$$
\textrm{DET:OLD}\%(G) \leq \frac{21}{22}.
$$

The bound would improve the general upper bound $\textrm{DET:OLD}\%(G) \leq \frac{30}{31}$ for cubic graphs that permit DET:OLD, and is motivated by the extremal cubic graphs found on $16$ through $24$ vertices. Whether $\frac{21}{22}$ is the tight upper bound for all relevant cubic graphs remains open.
358866.source_name: Devin Jean and Suk Seo, “On Error-detecting Open-locating-dominating sets”, arXiv:2306.12583 (2023).
358866.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12583

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

358982.title: The maximum odd-cycle and path likelihood conjecture
358982.statement:
Let $m\geq 3$, and let $\mu$ be an edge probability mass. For a graph $H$, write $\beta(\mu;H)$ for the total $\mu$-weight of copies of $H$, and let $C_m$ and $P_{m+1}$ denote the cycle on $m$ vertices and the path on $m+1$ vertices, respectively.

**Maximum likelihood conjecture.** For every $m\geq 3$ and every edge probability mass $\mu$,

$$
2m\cdot\beta(\mu;C_m)+\beta(\mu;P_{m+1})\leq {2\over m^{m-1}},
$$

with equality if and only if $\mu$ is the uniform distribution on $E(C_m)$.

The paper establishes a bound with constant $2.6947$ for $m\geq 5$, leaving the sharper constant $2$ and its equality characterization as the main question. The conjecture is therefore open.
358982.source_name: Emily Heath, Ryan R. Martin and Chris Wells, “The maximum number of odd cycles in a planar graph”, arXiv:2307.00116 (2023).
358982.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00116

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

359803.title: Miklavič–Šparl conjecture on non--distance-balanced generalized Petersen graphs
359803.statement:
Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer, and define

$$
n_k=\begin{cases}
11, & k=2,\\
(k+1)^2, & k\text{ is odd},\\
k(k+2), & k\ge 4\text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

For a graph $G$, write $D$ for its diameter. **Miklavič–Šparl conjecture.** For every $n>n_k$, the generalized Petersen graph $GP(n,k)$ is not $\ell$-distance-balanced for any integer $\ell$ with $1\le \ell<D$. Moreover, $n_k$ is the smallest integer with this property.
The conjecture concerns the intermediate distance levels of generalized Petersen graphs: although the cited work proved the assertion for $k=2$, the general case is presented here as a conjecture. The minimality assertion specifies the sharp threshold in $n$ for each value of $k$.
359803.source_name: Gang Ma, Jianfeng Wang and Sandi Klavžar, “Non--distance-balanced generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,3) and GP(n,4)”, arXiv:2309.01900 (2023).
359803.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2208.08305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08305).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01900

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360074.title: Equality and strict upper-bound conjecture for the estimates of direct powers of free distributive lattices
360074.statement:
Let $g_3^{\ast}(n)$, $g_3^{\ast\ast}(n)$, and $g_r(n)$ be the functions defined earlier in the paper, and let $\mathbb{N}^{\geq k}=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:n\geq k\}$. **Equality and strict upper-bound conjecture.** We guess that

$$
g_{3}^{\ast}(n)=g_{3}^{\ast\ast}(n)
$$

for all $n\in\mathbb{N}^{\geq 3}$, and that

$$
g_{3}^{\ast\ast}(n)<g_r(n)
$$

for all $n\in\mathbb{N}^{\geq 6}$. This conjecture concerns the comparison of the paper's computable estimates for the minimum size of generating sets of direct powers of free distributive lattices; the stated theorem establishes the corresponding equality only for $n\in\{3,4,\dots,300\}$ and the strict inequality only for $n\in\{5,6,\dots,300\}$, so the extensions to all indicated $n$ remain open.
360074.source_name: Gábor Czédli, “Minimum-sized generating sets of the direct powers of free distributive lattices”, arXiv:2309.13783 (2023).
360074.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.13783

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360293.title: The minimum-size conjecture for minimal uncolorable uniform bi-hypergraphs
360293.statement:
Let $m(r)$ be the smallest positive integer for which there exists a minimal uncolorable $r$-uniform bi-hypergraph with $m(r)$ edges. Complete $r$-uniform bi-hypergraphs on $(r-1)^2+1$ vertices have $\binom{(r-1)^2+1}{r}$ edges.

**Minimum-size conjecture.** For any $r\in \mathbb{N}$ with $r\ge 4$,

$$
m(r)=\binom{(r-1)^2+1}{r}.
$$

The conjecture predicts that the complete construction gives the smallest possible minimal uncolorable $r$-uniform bi-hypergraph for every $r\ge 4$. For $r=4$, the source reduces this to proving colorability of every $4$-uniform bi-hypergraph of order at most $49$ and size at most $209$; the general conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.
360293.source_name: Meiqiao Zhang, Fengming Dong and Ruixue Zhang, “On the colorability of bi-hypergraphs”, arXiv:2310.06464 (2023).
360293.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

362602.title: The initial log-concavity thresholds for k-th power partition functions
362602.statement:
For an integer $k\geq 2$, let $p^k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into perfect $k$-th powers. Define $N_k$ to be the smallest index such that the sequence $\{p^k(n)\}$ is log-concave for all $n>N_k$.

**Initial log-concavity threshold conjecture.** For $k\leq6$, the smallest such values are

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
p^k(n)&p^2(n)&p^3(n)&p^4(n)&p^5(n)&p^6(n)\\
\hline
N_k&1041&15655&637854&2507860&35577568
\end{array}
$$

These values record the first index after which log-concavity is observed for the square through sixth-power partition functions. The source gives no proof or resolution of this finite-data assertion.
362602.source_name: Arindam Roy, “Log-concavity And The Multiplicative Properties of Restricted Partition Functions”, arXiv:2404.03153 (2025).
362602.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03153

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

365438.title: Maximum preimage conjecture for the $1\underline{23}$ and $3\underline{21}$ stack-sorting maps
365438.statement:
Let $\mathfrak S_n$ be the set of permutations of length $n$, and let $\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}$ and $\text{SC}_{3\underline{21}}$ be the corresponding vincular-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting maps. **Maximum-preimage conjecture.** For every $n\ge 2$,

$$
\max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}|\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}^{-1}(\pi)|=\max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}|\text{SC}_{3\underline{21}}^{-1}(\pi)|=2^{n-2}.
$$

The claim gives the maximum possible preimage count for both maps. The surrounding paper develops bounds and related constructions, but the supplied text does not state a resolution of this assertion.
365438.source_name: William Zhao, “Stack-sorting with Stacks Avoiding Vincular Patterns”, arXiv:2410.17057 (2024).
365438.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

365716.title: Two-cluster convergence conjecture for causal transformer dynamics with simple dominant eigendirection
365716.statement:
Let $Q$ and $K$ be arbitrary matrices, and let $V$ be diagonalizable with $d$ different positive real eigenvalues. Denote its largest eigenvalue by $\lambda_{\max}$, and let $\xi$ be a unit eigenvector satisfying

$$
V\xi=\lambda_{\max}\xi.
$$

For the causal transformer dynamics, **two-cluster convergence conjecture.** For almost every starting point $(x_1(0),\ldots,x_n(0))$ with respect to the volume measure on $(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n$,

$$
\forall k\in[n],\qquad \lim_{t\to\infty}x_k(t)\in\\{\xi,-\xi\\}.
$$

This conjectures that, when the dominant eigenvalue is positive and has a one-dimensional eigendirection under the stated diagonalizability assumptions, causal attention generically drives all tokens into two antipodal clusters. The claim is presented as part of the paper's conjectural extension beyond the proved identity-matrix case; its resolution is not supplied here.
365716.source_name: Nikita Karagodin, Yury Polyanskiy and Philippe Rigollet, “Clustering in Causal Attention Masking”, arXiv:2411.04990 (2024).
365716.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04990

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “While a rigorous proof of this dimension-reduction remains an open problem for future investigation, this phenomenon motivates our focus on low-dimensional cases (specifically $d=2$) throughout this section.”

370598.title: Numerical threshold conjecture for cubic overpartition Jensen polynomials
370598.statement:
Let $\overline{a}(n)$ denote the cubic overpartition function, and define its Jensen polynomials by

$$
J_{\overline{a}}^{d,n}(X):=\sum_{i=0}^{d}\binom{d}{i}\overline{a}(n+i)X^i.
$$

For each degree $d$, let $N_{\overline{a}}(d)$ be the minimum integer such that $J_{\overline{a}}^{d,n-1}(X)$ is hyperbolic for all $n\geq N_{\overline{a}}(d)$. **The numerical threshold conjecture.** The observed threshold values are

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
d&3&4&5&6&7\\hline
N_{\overline{a}}(d)&39&89&172&279&423
\end{array}
$$

These values are based on numerical evidence from Mathematica; the source does not provide a proof or resolution of the conjecture.
370598.source_name: Archit Agarwal, Meghali Garg and Bibekananda Maji, “Rademacher-type exact formula and higher order Turán inequalities for cubic overpartitions”, arXiv:2509.23151 (2025).
370598.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23151

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2025). “This conjecture was settled by Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier .”

370763.title: Crofton-type conjecture for random Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
370763.statement:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a centered, time-symmetric, exhaustive or periodically exhaustive law-defining datum. Let $L\subset M$ be a closed Lagrangian submanifold. The datum specifies an almost complex structure $J$ and the associated Riemannian metric $g$.

**Crofton-type conjecture.** There exist a constant $C>0$ and a smooth function $\rho:M\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, depending only on $\mathcal{D}$ and $L$ and satisfying

$$
\int_M \rho\,\omega^n=\operatorname{vol}(M),
$$

such that, for every closed Lagrangian submanifold $K\subset M$,

$$
\int_{\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)} \#(L\cap\varphi(K))\,d\mu_{\operatorname{Ham}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\varphi)=C\cdot\operatorname{vol}_{\rho\cdot g}(K).
$$

In particular, there exist constants $C',C”>0$ such that

$$
C'\cdot\operatorname{vol}_g(K)\leq\int_{\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)}\#(L\cap\varphi(K))\,d\mu_{\operatorname{Ham}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\varphi)\leq C”\cdot\operatorname{vol}_g(K).
$$

The conjecture seeks a Crofton formula for expected Lagrangian intersection counts, with a density-rescaled metric accounting for the nonuniform behavior seen in simulations. The supplied text gives numerical evidence and explains why the standard metric does not yield an exact formula, but states no resolution; the conjecture remains open.
370763.source_name: Adrian Dawid, “Random Hamiltonians I: Probability measures and random walks on the Hamiltonian diffeomorphism group”, arXiv:2510.03190 (2025).
370763.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

371484.title: The extremal solvabilizer conjecture for finite groups
371484.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and define

$$
\operatorname{Solv}(G)=\{\operatorname{Sol}_G(x):x\in G\}.
$$

A composition factor of $G$ is a factor in a composition series of $G$.

**Extremal solvabilizer conjecture.** If

$$
|\operatorname{Solv}(G)|=32,
$$

then $G$ has a composition factor isomorphic to $A_5$.

The preceding theorem establishes the lower bound $|\operatorname{Solv}(G)|\geq 32$ for every nonsolvable finite group. Thus the conjecture concerns the equality case and asserts that the smallest possible nonsolvable value is explained by the occurrence of $A_5$ as a composition factor.
371484.source_name: Banafsheh Akbari, Ethan Han, Sasha Lin and Benjamin Vakil, “The Number of Solvabilizers in Finite Groups”, arXiv:2511.11544 (2025).
371484.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2403.08129](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08129).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

373717.title: The recursive bound for tone chromatic numbers of subcubic outerplanar graphs
373717.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic outerplanar graph, meaning that $G$ is outerplanar and has maximum degree at most $3$. For each positive integer $t$, let $\tau_t(G)$ denote the smallest number of colors in a $t$-tone coloring of $G$. **The recursive bound.** For every integer $t\ge 3$,

$$
\tau_t(G)\le \tau_{t-1}(G)+t+1.
$$

This is proposed as a relationship between successive tone chromatic numbers after the paper establishes the sharp bound $\tau_3(G)\le 11$ for subcubic outerplanar graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
373717.source_name: Hadeel Al Bazzal and Olivier Togni, “t-tone colorings of outerplanar and Halin graphs”, arXiv:2603.18674 (2026).
373717.references:

373910.title: Matching conjecture for the stochastic Bessel limiting point process
373910.statement:
For $a\geq 0$, let $\mathcal{M}_a=\sum_{i\geq 1}\delta_{\mu_a^{\infty}(i)}$ be the limiting point process, and let $(g_j)_{j\geq 1}$ be independent exponential random variables with parameters $j(j+a)/2$. Define

$$
\hat{\mu}_a^{\infty}(k):=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}g_j,\qquad k\geq 1.
$$

**Matching conjecture.** For all $a\geq 0$, the joint distributions of $(\hat{\mu}_a^{\infty}(i),\;i\geq 1)$ and $(\mu_a^{\infty}(i),\;i\geq 1)$ are equal. As a corollary, using the explicit expression for the density of $\hat{\mu}_a^{\infty}(1)$,

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{j-1}\frac{j(2j+a)}{2}\binom{j+a}{j}e^{-\frac{j(j+a)}{2}x},
$$

this matching yields

$$
\mathbb{P}\big(\exists t\geq 0,\;R^{-a}(t)\geq\mu+bt\big)=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{j-1}\left[\binom{j+a/b}{j}+\binom{j+a/b-1}{j-1}\right]e^{-2\mu j(jb+a)},
$$

where $R^{-a}$ is a reflected Brownian motion with drift $-a$.

The conjecture extends the proved equality of the largest points at $a=0$ to the entire point process and all $a\geq 0$. If true, it would provide an unexpected diffusion representation of the exponential-gap construction and an exact formula for the hitting probability of a reflected Brownian motion with negative drift.
373910.source_name: Laure Dumaz and Hugo Magaldi, “The spectrum of the stochastic Bessel operator at high temperature”, arXiv:2603.27602 (2026).
373910.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

374578.title: Finite area determination conjecture for Kähler–Einstein metrics on a product of surfaces
374578.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be the closed surface under consideration, let $\mathcal L^*(g)$ denote the relevant set of surface subgroups of genus $g$, and let $A(h)(\Pi)$ be the associated area function of a metric $h$ on $\Sigma\times\Sigma$. **Finite area determination conjecture.** There is a finite set $\mathcal L_0\subset\mathcal L^*(g)$ such that, if $h$ and $\hat h$ are Kähler–Einstein metrics on $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ satisfying

$$
A(h)(\Pi)=A(\hat h)(\Pi)\quad\text{for all }\Pi\in\mathcal L_0,
$$

then $h$ and $\hat h$ are isometric, and the isometry is homotopic to the identity. This asks whether finitely many minimal-Lagrangian area measurements determine a Kähler–Einstein metric up to an isometry homotopic to the identity; the supplied text presents it as a new question, with no resolution stated.
374578.source_name: Ben Lowe, Fernando C. Marques and André Neves, “Counting Minimal Lagrangians Via Mirzakhani Functions”, arXiv:2605.04614 (2026).
374578.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04614

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

378132.title: The orbit lattice conjecture for platycosms
378132.statement:
A **platycosm** $P$ is a compact flat three-dimensional manifold. Its **orbit lattice bound** $R_0$ is the maximum of the covering radii of all orbit lattices for $P$, and $P$ has the **orbit lattice property** if its diameter equals $R_0$.

**Orbit lattice conjecture for platycosms.** All 10 platycosms have the orbit lattice property.

The orbit lattice bound gives a lower bound for the diameter of every platycosm; when an orbit lattice has a translatable Voronoi tiling, the bound is attained. The conjecture asserts that this equality holds for all 10 platycosms.
378132.source_name: John Horton Conway and Juan Pablo Rossetti, “Describing the platycosms”, arXiv:math/0311476 (2003).
378132.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311476

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2003).

381055.title: Pemantle's conjecture that CNC implies CNA
381055.statement:
Let $cmu
a$ be a probability measure on $c{0,1}^n$. It is **CNC** if every pair of disjoint increasing events is negatively correlated, and it is **CNA** if every pair of disjoint subsets of coordinates has negatively associated restrictions under conditioning on any increasing function of the remaining coordinates. In the setting of generalized urn measures, write $R^+$ for the property that every external field transformation $W\circ\mu$, with $W_i\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ for all $i$, is negatively correlated.

**Pemantle's conjecture.** CNC implies CNA. In particular, the equivalent formulation considered here is that $R^+$ implies CNA.

The conjecture asks whether the stronger conditional negative association property follows from conditional negative correlation. The paper notes that a negative answer for generalized urn measures would provide a counterexample to the CNC-implies-CNA conjecture, and that CNC for this class is equivalent to the stated $R^+$ property; its resolution is not supplied here.
381055.source_name: Jeff Kahn and Michael Neiman, “Conditional negative association for competing urns”, arXiv:1001.0610 (2010).
381055.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.0610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2010).

382271.title: Distinct spectral radii for Type 5 digraphs
382271.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $5\leq n$, and let $r_k,s_k,t_k$ satisfy

$$
4\leq r_k\leq s_k\leq t_k<n,\qquad r_k+s_k+t_k=2n,
$$

for $k=1,2$, with $(r_1,s_1,t_1)\neq(r_2,s_2,t_2)$. For each $k$, let $\rho_k$ be the only real positive root of

$$
x^n-x^{n-r_k}-x^{n-s_k}-x^{n-t_k}-2.
$$

**Distinct-root conjecture.** One has $\rho_1\neq\rho_2$. This asserts that distinct admissible parameter triples determine distinct spectral radii for the corresponding Type $5$ digraphs. The claim was computationally verified for $5\leq n\leq 200$; the conjecture proposes that it holds for every $n\geq5$.
382271.source_name: Diego Bravo, Florencia Cubría, Marcelo Fiori and Gustavo Rama, “Some families of digraphs determined by the complementarity spectrum”, arXiv:2403.10665 (2024).
382271.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10665

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

384622.title: Gaussian heat-smoothing: a weaker form
384622.statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$ and $1< p < \infty$. Show that there exists $c_p>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all polynomials $f\in \text{Lin}\{x^k,k\ge d\}$, we have
	

$$
\|Nf\|_p\ge dc_p\|f\|_p,
$$

	where $N=\Delta-x\nabla$ is the generator of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup.
384622.source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing (posed by Paata Ivanisvili)

384631.title: Pathological sets (problem 4)
384631.statement: Does the existence of a set $E$ such that $E$ is not $\sigma$-finite in dimension $1$ but for every superlinear gauge function $\varphi$, $H_\varphi(E) = 0$ imply that there is a counterexample to the Borel conjecture?
384631.source_name: AimPL: Effective methods in measure and dimension (posed by Ted Slaman)

386245.title: Cycle + Erdos-Renyi
386245.statement:
Prove that for $p=\frac \epsilon n$, $\epsilon>0$ fixed, the nonreversible chain has $t_{\text{mix}}\asymp \log n$.

Prove that when $p=\epsilon n^{-\frac 32}$ the nonreversible chain has $t_{\text{mix}}=\tilde O(\sqrt n)$.
386245.source_name: AimPL: Markov chain mixing times (posed by Balazs Gerencser)

387366.title: Some Questions — Question 13
387366.statement: For a graph sequence $(G_n)$ define $e((G_n))=\liminf |E(G_n)|/|V(G_n)|$, and define its combinatorial cost as the infimum of $e((H_n))$ over graph sequences $(H_n)$ on the same vertex sets for which the identity maps have uniformly bounded bi-Lipschitz constants. If $(G_n)$ and $(H_n)$ converge locally to the same limit, must they have the same combinatorial cost?

387928.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.76
387928.statement: Prove or disprove the following statement: If $K$ is a compact subset of $\mathbb{C}$ with continuous analytic capacity $\alpha(K)= 0$, then \[\alpha(E\setminus K)=\alpha(E)\] for all compact subsets $E$ of $\mathbb{C}$. An interesting special case is when $K$ is a $C^1$-arc. The case when $K$ is a $C^{1+\varepsilon}$-arc has already been settled. (A. G. O'Farrell)
387928.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

388439.title: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 17
388439.statement: Suppose that the polynomials $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\in \mathbb Z[t]$ are rationally independent and have zero constant term. Show that for every $A\in \mathcal X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $n\in \mathbb N$ such that $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap \cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A)\geq \mu(A)^{\ell+1}-\varepsilon. $$

389482.title: Converse implications among SIRSN properties
389482.statement: Prove or disprove each of the proposed implications between the SIRSN properties numbered (16), (20), (49), (50), and (51): (16)$\Rightarrow$(20), unique singly-infinite geodesics$\Rightarrow$(49), (49)$\Rightarrow$(50), and (51)$\Rightarrow$(50).

396247.title: Stability of unitary representations and amenability
396247.statement: Does the conjunction of the two stability properties described in the report characterize amenability for discrete groups: (i) unitary $\varepsilon$-representations are uniformly close to unitary representations, and (ii) uniformly close pairs of unitary representations are conjugate by a unitary operator close to the identity?

402384.title: Relative local character-expansion homogeneity conjecture
402384.statement:
For all $r\in\mathbb{R}$, the restriction identity $(\mathrm{RLCE}^{\wedge})$ holds:
\[
\operatorname{res}\!\mid_{D(V)_{r+}}\widetilde{J}(V)_{r+}=\operatorname{res}\!\mid_{D(V)_{r+}}J(N_V).
\]
